I ran a funding analysis across all three of your goals — here's where each really stands.

**Lake house** — your big one. Target **$350,000**, about four years out. You're **32% funded** (~$112K today), and at a normal growth rate that projects to roughly **$141K by your horizon — about a $209,000 gap.** Closing it on time would take around **$3,856/month**, or easing the timeline. The recent spending running ~18% over plan is the main thing working against it.

**Grandkids' 529s** — $120,000 target, 18% funded, but a 10-year runway, so far less urgent (about $500/month closes it).

**Retirement income** — the $9,000/month draw — is **on track** in the base case.

So: **1 of 3 goals on track**, with the lake house the one to focus on. None of this is a verdict — it's the math laid out. Want me to show what closes the lake-house gap, or flag it for Dana?
